results.title: Cognitive Definition and Meaning in Psychology
results.content: Some of the many different cognitive processes include thinking, knowing, remembering, judging, and [problem-solving](https://www.verywellmind.com/problem-solving-2795008). [Attention](https://www.verywellmind.com/what-is-attention-2795009) is a cognitive process that allows people to focus on a specific environmental stimulus. [Learning](https://www.verywellmind.com/what-is-learning-2795332) requires cognitive processes involved in taking in new things, synthesizing information, and integrating it with prior knowledge. [Memory](https://www.verywellmind.com/what-is-memory-2795006) is an important cognitive process that allows people to encode, store, and retrieve information. [Perception](https://www.verywellmind.com/perception-and-the-perceptual-process-2795839) is a cognitive process that allows people to take in information through their senses, then utilize this information to respond and interact with the world. Hot cognition refers to mental processes in which emotion plays a role, such as [reward-based learning](https://www.verywellmind.com/what-is-positive-reinforcement-2795412). [Cognitive biases](https://www.verywellmind.com/what-is-a-cognitive-bias-2794963) are systematic errors in thinking related to how people process and interpret information about the world. Researchers and educators use their knowledge of these cognitive processes to create instructive materials to help people [learn new concepts](https://www.verywellmind.com/how-to-become-a-more-effective-learner-2795162). How we remember, what we remember, and [what we forget](https://www.verywellmind.com/forgetting-about-psychology-2795034) reveal a great deal about how cognitive processes operate.
